Article Title: Government set to halt sugarcane juice, B-heavy molasses diversion for ethanol
Article Text:
File photo: Sugarcane at a market, in Guwahati

NEW DELHI: Government is set to disallow diversion of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses for ethanol production in the 2026-27 ethanol supply year (ESY) starting November, amid an around 11% shortfall in sugar production from initial estimates for the 2025-26 sugar season and indications of a further decline in output due to drought in major sugarcane-growing states of Maharashtra and Karnataka.TOI has learnt that government will notify the decision soon, ahead of the start of the new ESY. While ethanol supply year runs from Nov 1 to Oct 31, sugar season in India runs from Oct 1 to Sep 30. Government specifies the quantity of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses that can be diverted for ethanol production to meet the mandatory blending target for the green fuel in petrol.The move comes at a time when domestic sugar supplies remain tight. Mills diverted about 30 lakh tonnes of sugar, or around 10% of total output, for ethanol production during the sugar season that ended on September 30. The new sugar season began on October 1 with opening stocks of around 37.5 lakh tonnes, compared with nearly 50 lakh tonnes a year ago.Industry sources said there was no scope for allowing further diversion of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses for ethanol, as ensuring adequate domestic sugar supplies remains a priority for both govt and mills.With the possibility of a fall in output in the current season, particularly in Maharashtra and Karnataka, government would prioritise sugar availability over additional diversion for ethanol.Disallowing the use of sugarcane juice, syrup and B-heavy molasses for ethanol in 2026-27 would enable mills to produce more sugar from the available cane, helping augment domestic supplies and meeting consumption requirements.Government has said that the share of sugar diverted for ethanol has declined from around 12% in 2022-23 to around 9% in 2025-26. Besides, nearly three-fourths of ethanol produced in the country now comes from grains, particularly maize, reducing the dependence on sugar-based feedstock.“Meeting the demand for 20% ethanol blending in petrol won’t be an issue. With indications of millers getting a better price, it won’t be a problem for them either. Government would have to continue with the ban on exports and may have to allow more imports as well,” an industry analyst said.Sugar production in the 2025-26 season was hit by crop diseases, waterlogging and adverse weather in key producing states. Against the initial production estimate of around 343 lakh tonnes, output was estimated at around 306 lakh tonnes in August, including the quantity diverted for ethanol production.After accounting for the diversion to ethanol, net sugar production in 2025-26 was around 279 lakh tonnes, barely enough to meet the normative domestic consumption requirement of 280-285 lakh tonnes.
Article Summary: Government is set to disallow diversion of sugarcane juice, syrup and b-heavy molasses for ethanol production in the 2026-27 ethanol supply year (esy) the move comes amid an around 11% shortfall in sugar production from initial estimates for the 2025-26 sugar season.

Hyderabad turned into a global meeting point for the real estate sector as the 7th International Real Estate Conference (IREC 2026) brought together more than 2,000 delegates from over 35 countries at HITEX from September 25 to 27.The three-day conference, hosted by the Hyderabad Realtors Association (HRA) with the National Association of REALTORS®–India (NAR-India) as a strategic partner, brought developers, institutional investors, realtors, policymakers, technology leaders and property professionals onto a common platform.The event brought together the Global Conference, IREC Luxury Property Expo and Innovation Showcase, with discussions spanning institutional investment, changing buyer behaviour, branded residences, holiday homes, affordable housing, real estate tokenisation, cross-border transactions and the growing role of PropTech, artificial intelligence, data and DeepTech.One of the key highlights of the conference was the launch of the India Housing Report – September 2026, prepared by NAR and CRE Matrix. Based on H1 2026 data, the report put the value of primary housing sales across India's Tier-I cities at ₹3.63 lakh crore, broadly unchanged from the record level recorded in H1 2025.According to the report, 2.58 lakh housing units were sold during the first half of 2026, a decline of around 2% year-on-year, while new launches rose about 7% to 2.98 lakh units.The Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) remained the largest housing market, accounting for around 26% of pan-India housing value, followed by NCR at 19%. MMR recorded approximately ₹93,800 crore in primary housing sales.Navi Mumbai and Raigad recorded 29% growth in housing value, with volumes rising around 20%, while Bengaluru recorded 25% growth in housing value and accounted for approximately 17% of the national housing value.IREC 2026 featured participation and perspectives from markets including the US, Dubai, Philippines, Georgia, Canada, Japan, Mongolia, China, Korea, Taiwan, Cambodia, Indonesia and Vietnam.The discussions focused on strengthening India's integration with global real estate markets, attracting institutional and international investment, facilitating cross-border transactions and exploring the creation of a more connected global real estate marketplace.The conference was inaugurated by Majid Saqer Al Marri, Real Estate Registration & Services, Dubai Land Department, while Kevin Brown, President, National Association of REALTORS® (NAR), inaugurated the IREC Luxury Property Expo.For Hyderabad, the conference provided a platform to examine the city's real estate growth against the backdrop of international investment, urbanisation and technology-led transformation.Speaking at the inauguration, Sumanth Reddy, Chairman, NAR-India, said the real estate sector was changing faster than the traditional transaction cycle, with increasingly informed buyers, more global capital flows and technology reshaping the way business is conducted.Mr. D.Sridhar Reddy, Founder & Past President - HRA and NAR-INDIA, said hosting IREC in Hyderabad was aimed at placing the city in a wider global real estate conversation and ensuring that discussions remained practical and relevant to professionals across markets.Shailender Singh, Chairman, IREC 2026, said changing buyer preferences, cross-border investment and emerging technologies were creating new opportunities as well as new questions for the industry.The conference also featured sessions on Dubai's real estate model, institutional investment, India's growth opportunities, affordable housing, tokenisation, branded residences, urban development and the future of PropTech and DeepTech, alongside the Luxury Property Expo and Innovation Showcase.

India housing report – september 2026, valued primary housing sales across tier-i cities at ₹3.63 lakh crore in h1 2026.

Article Title: India successfully demonstrates its first free-space quantum-secure communication link for over 5.5 km
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Indian deep-tech startup QNu Labs, in collaboration with Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo-informatics (BISAG-N) and IIT Gandhinagar, has successfully demonstrated India’s first free-space quantum key distribution (QKD) link for over 5.56 km.A free-space QKD link is an ultra-secure way to share secret digital passwords using particles of light travelling through open air or space instead of a physical fibre-optic cable. It uses quantum mechanics principles, and any attempt by an outsider to intercept or measure the photons changes their state; therefore, it is the most secure form of sending data. Traditional QKD is limited by signal loss inside fibre-optic cables, whereas free-space links allow communication across open terrain, water or obstacles where laying cables is difficult. Free-space optics form the foundational bridge for transmitting keys between Earth and orbiting satellites and create the backbone for a global, quantum-secure internet network.“The field trial, conducted on the night of Sept 27–28, established a secure quantum communication channel between BISAG-N and IIT-G,” the IT and electronics ministry said in a statement on Saturday.Using QNu Labs’ pointing, acquisition and tracking system, the trial achieved a stable quantum bit error rate below 5% and generated secure keys at a rate of 230–260 bps.These keys were integrated with BISAG-N’s post-quantum cryptography-enabled Vedic Kavach platform, enabling successful end-to-end encryption and decryption of test messages.Vinay Thakur, director general, BISAG-N, said the integration of Vedic Kavach with QNu Labs’ QKD technology marks a significant step towards practical quantum-resilient communication systems. Sunil Gupta, co-founder and CEO, QNu Labs, emphasised that the successful 5.56 km demonstration paves the way for longer-distance quantum-secure networks and satellite-based quantum communication.Cmde Manish Tripathi (Retd.), In-charge, ISTF, IIT Gandhinagar, said the demonstration provides a valuable field environment for advancing practical quantum communication technologies and showcases how academia, indigenous technology and real-world experimentation can be integrated to meet emerging secure communication requirements. The trial provides a foundation for advancing India’s capabilities in secure communication infrastructure, strengthening resilience against emerging quantum-era security threats.
Article Summary: Indian deep-tech startup qnu labs has demonstrated india’s first free-space quantum key distribution (qkd) link for over 5.56 km. Free-space qkd is an ultra-secure way to share secret digital passwords using particles of light travelling through open air or space.

Article Title: 300 students take on AI, deepfake fraud challenges at BIT Mesra hackathon
Article Text:

RANCHI: More than 300 students from Birla Institute of Technology (BIT) Mesra took part in in a 24-hour hackathon focused on some of the most pressing challenges emerging from the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence, including high-precision generative AI systems, deepfake-driven insurance fraud and agentic AI applications.The event, Adrosonic Build, organised by technology company Adrosonic, has attracted 106 teams comprising around three students each. Twenty-one teams have been shortlisted for the final round, which began on October 3 and will conclude with the announcement of results on October 4.Unlike conventional coding competitions, the hackathon is centred on real-world industry problems. Participants are developing solutions for high-precision Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, AI-powered detection of synthetic identities and deepfake-based insurance claims, and agentic Statement of Values (SOV) intelligence systems for the insurance sector.Highlighting the broader objective of the initiative, Mayank, founder, CEO and MD of Adrosonic, said the idea was to bring practical industry knowledge, real-world use cases and access to technology leaders into the academic ecosystem so that students can work on problems that mirror actual business and societal challenges.Faculty members say such platforms are becoming increasingly important as employers seek graduates who can apply technical knowledge to complex situations rather than merely demonstrate theoretical understanding.“The gap is not in knowledge. It is in applying that knowledge to real-life scenarios, which are more uncertain and complex,” said Dr Manish Kumar Pandey, head of the Digital Innovation Lab and Department of Quantitative Economics and Data Science at BIT Mesra.The hackathon is part of a wider industry-academia partnership between Adrosonic and BIT Mesra that has been underway since 2022. The collaboration led to the establishment of the Digital Innovation Lab (DIL) in 2024, with an investment of around Rs 5 crore. The facility provides students access to infrastructure and technologies spanning artificial intelligence, machine learning, large language models and data science.Over the past two years, the partnership has expanded through fellowship programmes, industry-led initiatives and mentorship opportunities, allowing students to engage with professionals and gain exposure to practical technology applications beyond the classroom.“A hackathon gives students the opportunity to test their theories against real challenges, while building teamwork, problem-solving and execution skills,” said Kamlesh Yadav, head of innovation at Adrosonic.The event was inaugurated on October 2 in the presence of senior faculty members, including Prof Vishal H Shah, associate dean, alumni and international relations, and Dr Kishore Kumar Sinapati, along with representatives from Adrosonic. As teams race against time to build and present working solutions, the hackathon offers a glimpse into how institutes are preparing students for an AI-driven future.
Article Summary: More than 300 students from birla institute of technology (bit) mesra took part in in a 24-hour hackathon. The event, adrosonic build, has attracted 106 teams comprising around three students each. Twenty-one teams have been shortlisted for the final round, which began on october 3.

Article Title: Nestle dairy whitener found unsafe, substandard by FSSAI; Nestle says product safe
Article Text:
A Nestlé India spokesperson said phosphorus occurs naturally in milk and is therefore present in milk-based products

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A sample of Nestlé India’s Low Fat Dairy Whitener, collected from the premises of The LaLiT in Connaught Place, has been declared “unsafe and substandard” by a Food Analyst’s laboratory, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said on Saturday.The sample was collected from M/s Bharat Hotels Ltd (The LaLiT), Connaught Place, FSSAI said. The regulator said the Food Analyst’s report found the product non-compliant under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.FSSAI said a copy of the laboratory analysis report was provided to the food business operator and a notice was issued regarding the non-compliant product. The operator was given an opportunity to appeal against the Food Analyst’s report within the prescribed period. FSSAI also directed that the identified product be immediately prohibited from sale.However, Nestlé India said the product is safe to consume and complies with all applicable regulatory requirements.A Nestlé India spokesperson said phosphorus occurs naturally in milk and is therefore present in milk-based products. The company said the FSSAI laboratory report reflects total phosphorus against the additive limit without accounting for the substantial natural phosphorus contribution from milk-based ingredients.Nestlé said the product is in full compliance with prescribed limits for added phosphorus under the Food Safety and Standards Regulations, including on an “as consumed” basis. The company said it has been engaging with the authorities through the due process established under law and has shared data on other same or similar milk-based products to demonstrate the presence of naturally occurring phosphorus.The LaLiT said the product was a packaged product procured from Nestlé India and that the sample was collected by FSSAI from the hotel approximately three months ago.Vivek Shukla, CEO, The LaLiT Suri Hospitality Group, said that after receiving communication from FSSAI, the hotel immediately took up the matter with Nestlé India, which assured it that the company would respond directly to FSSAI.The hotel said it simultaneously discontinued use of the product and removed all packets from its operations.“The matter concerning the product’s compliance is between FSSAI and Nestlé India and not with The LaLiT,” Shukla said, adding that the hotel had acted promptly after receiving the communication and remained committed to food safety protocols and compliance with FSSAI regulations.FSSAI’s public communication does not specify the particular laboratory finding or parameter that led to the sample being classified as unsafe and substandard.
Article Summary: A sample of nestlé india’s low fat dairy whitener has been declared ‘unsafe and substandard’ the sample was collected from m/s bharat hotels ltd (the lalit), connaught place. Nestlé said the product is safe to consume and complies with all applicable regulatory requirements.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: Lpg consumption in sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (mt), compared to 2.9 mt during the same month a year earlier. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in july. Erratic monsoon conditions due to el nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.

Article Title: Caitlin Clark’s Excel connection raises questions as Linda Cohn challenges WNBA commissioner search safeguards
Article Text:
Caitlin Clark’s Excel connection raises questions as Linda Cohn challenges WNBA commissioner search safeguards

Linda Cohn questions Excel’s role in the WNBA commissioner search

Excel Search & Advisory has WNBA ties as Cathy Engelbert prepares to leave

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The NBA has hired Excel Search & Advisory to help find Cathy Engelbert’s successor as WNBA commissioner, but the choice has already raised questions about possible conflicts of interest. Excel’s parent company, Excel Sports Management, represents WNBA stars Caitlin Clark and Napheesa Collier. Former ESPN host Linda Cohn has now asked how the company will keep its player representation work separate from the executive search as the league prepares for a major leadership change.Cohn focused on the connection between Excel and Caitlin Clark, whose rise has brought major attention to the WNBA. She said the situation deserves clear answers because the same wider company represents players while its search arm is helping identify the person who could lead the league.“Caitlin Clark isn’t just another client,” Cohn said in a video posted on her YouTube channel. “We are talking about a player whose arrival helped accelerate an extraordinary period of attention and business growth around this league. And now an arm of the company that represents her is helping identify the next commissioner of that league.”Cohn also pointed to Excel’s representation of other WNBA players, including Napheesa Collier, and said the league should explain how the two sides of the business will be kept apart.“So I think there’s a completely fair question to ask here. How separate are these operations? What safeguards are in place?” Cohn said. “Who inside Excel Search and Advisory has access to information about these candidates, and who doesn’t, for that matter? Is there a firewall between the executive search business and the agents representing WNBA players? … These are questions that need answers.”The concern is about the process, not a claim that Excel has acted improperly. Public reports have not established that information from the commissioner search has been shared with Excel’s player representation business.Excel Search & Advisory is the executive search arm of Excel Sports Management. According to Sports Business Journal, the NBA hired the firm to lead the search, while NBA Commissioner Adam Silver will make the final decision on Engelbert’s replacement.The timing is important because Engelbert announced on September 4 that she will retire at the end of 2026 after seven years as commissioner. The WNBA said her tenure included major growth in viewership, attendance, League Pass subscriptions, merchandise sales, sponsorship revenue and franchise values.Excel also has business ties with several WNBA teams. Reports say the company has worked on jersey patch partnerships involving the Atlanta Dream, Los Angeles Sparks and Dallas Wings, while its executive search business has helped professional sports organizations with senior hiring.That makes the company familiar with the league and its wider business structure, but it also explains why Cohn wants more clarity about how the search will be handled.For now, Excel’s job is to identify and vet candidates. The final choice remains with Adam Silver and the NBA Board of Governors. The WNBA has not publicly detailed specific safeguards for separating Excel’s search work from its player representation business.
Article Summary: Excel search & advisory is the executive search arm of excel sports management. The parent company represents wnba stars caitlin clark and napheesa collier. Former espn host linda cohn has asked how the company will keep its player representation work separate from the exec search.

Maria Sharapova’s financial journey didn’t end when she retired from professional tennis in 2020. The five-time Grand Slam champion had already amassed a large commercial profile during her playing career, with endorsements and business ventures supplementing her tennis earnings. Sharapova made $325 million before taxes during her career, which included endorsement income, Forbes reported.The most obvious example of her leap into entrepreneurship was her candy company, Sugarpova, which she founded in 2012. Article Title: In 2013, a New Jersey teacher saw workers mowing a solar field near home and asked to bring in her sheep; by 2021, her flock had grown from 50 sheep on 15 solar acres to 450 sheep managing 85 acres
Article Text:
Bishop's journey into solar grazing began at her six-acre farm in Newfield, New Jersey. With limited pasture available and a growing need for space for her sheep, she began looking for alternative grazing land.

From six acres to solar fields

Sheep as solar-site workers

A business that keeps expanding

Building a wider solar-grazing community

What began with a simple observation beside a solar field turned into an unusual farming business in New Jersey. When Julie Bishop noticed workers repeatedly mowing vegetation beneath and around solar panels, she saw an opportunity to put her sheep to work instead. A small flock grazing a single site eventually grew into a full-time solar-grazing operation, pairing livestock with renewable-energy infrastructure, according to an online observation piece by the Cornell University’s College of Agriculture and Life Sciences.According to the report, Bishop's journey into solar grazing began at her six-acre farm in Newfield, New Jersey. With limited pasture available and a growing need for space for her sheep, she began looking for alternative grazing land.A fenced solar array caught her attention. Instead of relying on machinery to keep vegetation under control, the site could be managed naturally by grazing animals. Bishop approached the solar company and eventually secured a vegetation-management contract. Solar Sheep LLC was born from that arrangement. The operation initially involved around 50 sheep grazing 15 acres of solar panels. By 2021, Bishop was managing approximately 85 acres across multiple solar sites with a flock of 450 sheep.As per the report, solar grazing requires considerably more planning than simply turning livestock loose in a field. Bishop uses portable fencing where a site allows it, creating paddocks that can be rotated as the flock moves through the vegetation. Not every solar installation is suited to extensive fencing, however. At smaller or awkwardly shaped sites, she relies on water and mineral stations to encourage the sheep to move toward areas that need attention. Transport is also an important part of the operation. Bishop uses a 24-foot stock trailer capable of carrying about 50 sheep at a time, while her Australian Cattle Dog, Mandy, helps gather the flock and locate animals during moves between sites.The flock consists primarily of mature yearlings and ewes. Lambs remain at the home farm, where Bishop can closely monitor their health and development. She raises Katahdin sheep, with lambing generally taking place in January and February. The resulting lambs are sold for meat, pets and to other solar grazers.The growing operation has also taken Bishop beyond routine vegetation management. Her experience has led to involvement in the planning of a proposed 700-acre utility-scale solar facility designed specifically for grazing. The planned site includes infrastructure such as lambing barns, feed storage, water and electricity, allowing sheep to remain on the property throughout the year. Bishop's expanding flock was expected to approach 1,000 animals as the operation developed.Solar grazing still comes with practical complications. Trucks and trailers must navigate sites that were often designed for equipment rather than livestock, while gates, cable trays and electrical infrastructure require careful coordination.Bishop became a member of the American Solar Grazing Association, finding value in a network focused on sharing knowledge and improving the way livestock and solar installations can coexist. Her experience also brought her a position as an ASGA board advisor, taking her work beyond her own flock. What started as a vision of sheep-shaped potential in a field of solar panels has emerged as a model for how farming and renewable-energy infrastructure can co-exist on the same land.Image Courtesy: Cornell University’s College of Agriculture and Life Sciences
Article Summary: Julie bishop's journey into solar grazing began at her six-acre farm in newfield, new jersey. With limited pasture available and a growing need for space for her sheep, she began looking for alternative grazing land. By 2021, bishop was managing approximately 85 acres across multiple solar sites with a flock of 450 sheep.

Article Title: Bombay HC to X: Remove video against Serum Institute, Adar Poonawalla
Article Text:
Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to take down a recent video uploaded by Yohan Tengra.





MUMBAI: Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to remove a video against Serum Institute of India Pvt Ltd and its CEO Adar Poonawalla that was uploaded by a social media influencer Yohan Tengra immediately after its June 5, 2023 order.Justice Gauri Godse of HC on Tuesday passed the order on SII and Poonawalla’s interim application in the pending defamation suit regarding content posted against the company and its COVID-19 vaccine. She also issued show-cause notices to Tengra, his organisation Anarchy for Freedom India, Ambar Koiri and TV 10 L.I.V.E, an online news portal, as to why action should not be taken for defying HC’s order. The notices are returnable on Oct 27.The application said Tengra and four defendants were restrained by the June 5, 2023 order from publishing or circulating defamatory videos and content. The same night Tengra uploaded a fresh video. On June 9, 2023, the plaintiffs issued a takedown notice to Google and X. Google complied but X refused, stating HC’s order was not issued against it.Advocate Karl Tamboly, for SII and Poonawalla, said videos uploaded were held to be unlawful by the June 5, 2023 order.Hence, videos and content of a like nature are also directed to be removed. He said in the absence of Tengra complying with HC’s direction, X is obligated to remove the objectionable content. Advocate Mayur Khandeparkar, for X, said the plaintiffs must initiate contempt proceedings against the defendants instead of waging a proxy battle with an intermediary.Justice Godse said it is undisputed that the objectionable content is still available with X. Tengra uploaded the fresh video not only in blatant defiance of HC’s injunction order “but he also states that he will not comply with the directions of the court and that he would not stop calling plaintiff no. 2 (Poonawalla) ‘a mass murderer’.”The judge noted there were no directions to X to remove the objectionable content and, thus, it cannot be held liable for the objectionable content not removed by the five defendants or for the new content uploaded by Tengra. Citing a Supreme Court judgment, she said even if an intermediary is exempt from liability for third-party information, necessary directions can be issued to remove the unlawful or prohibited content.Considering the “subsequent circumstance” of Tengra uploading the fresh video, Justice Godse said sufficient grounds are made out to direct X to “remove, delete or disable access” to the fresh video uploaded by Tengra.
Article Summary: Bombay high court has directed x corp to remove a video against serum institute of india pvt ltd and its ceo adar poonawalla. The video was uploaded by social media influencer yohan tengra immediately after its june 5, 2023 order. Justice gauri godse of hc on tuesday passed the order on an interim application in the pending defamation suit.

Article Title: India's factory growth hits 7 month high in September, thanks to demand and hiring boost
Article Text:
Factory growth hits 7-month high, PMI rises to 55.1

India’s manufacturing activity scaled up sharply in September, as stronger demand pushed up sales and production, while companies stepped up hiring and stock-building.The seasonally adjusted HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 55.1 in September, from 52.8 in August, marking the strongest improvement in the sector’s health in seven months. A PMI reading above 50 indicates expansion, while a reading below 50 signals contraction.The recovery in factory activity was supported by both domestic and overseas demand. Stronger new orders helped drive production higher, with demand across electronics, food, pharma and textiles taking total sales growth to its highest level since February.Export orders also gained momentum during the month, with manufacturers reporting increased business from clients in Brazil, Europe, the UAE and the US."India's factory sector ended the quarter on a firmer footing. The PMI rose to 55.1 in September, up from 52.8, as stronger domestic and overseas demand lifted sales and production. Hiring resumed at its fastest pace since May, and manufacturers became more optimistic about the months ahead," Pranjul Bhandari, chief India economist at HSBC, told PTI.The improvement in demand was accompanied by a renewed increase in factory employment.After a blip in August, job growth resumed in September, with the pace of employment expansion described by panellists as solid and the strongest since May.Manufacturers also became more confident about the months ahead. Output forecasts were upgraded during September, taking overall positive sentiment to a four-month high. The outlook was supported by a healthy pipeline of new enquiries and expectations that strong demand would continue.The expectation of higher future sales also prompted companies to increase their purchases of materials and build inventories. Overall buying activity expanded at a faster pace than in August."Companies bought more materials and built up stocks to prepare for anticipated sales. Finished goods inventories recorded their second-largest increase in nearly 12 years, signalling a clear shift from leaner stock levels," Bhandari said.Finished goods inventories rose for the third consecutive month. The increase was the second-fastest in 11-and-a-half years, behind July, as manufacturers actively accumulated stocks in anticipation of stronger demand.At the same time, companies faced quicker increases in input costs and selling prices. Despite the acceleration, the rates of inflation remained mild by historical standards.The September reading came as manufacturing activity regained momentum after the slower expansion recorded in August, with the PMI rising by more than two points during the month."Holdings of finished products increased for the third month in a row and at the second-fastest pace in 11-and-a-half years (behind July)," the report said.The HSBC India Manufacturing PMI is compiled by S&P Global based on responses from purchasing managers at around 400 manufacturers.
Article Summary: Factory growth hits 7-month high, pmi rises to 55.1. Stronger demand pushed up sales and production, while companies stepped up hiring and stock-building. Hiring resumed at its fastest pace since may, and manufacturers became more optimistic about the months ahead.

Article Title: Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses
Article Text:
Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses

Revenue growth draws investor attention

Huge infrastructure spending

Losses add to valuation questions

Customer concentration remains a risk

Anthropic has put a massive price tag on the AI boom, backing it with an equally heavy spending plan.The AI giant is heading towards a potential valuation of more than $2 trillion even as it plans $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations in the coming years.The company’s IPO prospectus, seen by Reuters, also shows just how quickly its business has grown. Anthropic’s revenue reportedly rose 12-fold in 2025, giving investors a strong growth story to weigh against its continuing losses and huge infrastructure commitments.The scale of its plans has also spilled into markets, with European technology shares rising 2.4% and the US chip index gaining 1.5%.For investors, Anthropic’s rapid expansion is a key part of the valuation story.Michael Field, chief equity strategist at Morningstar, Amsterdam, said the speed of the company’s growth stood out in the prospectus."If anything, the acceleration of the business is the biggest part of this release. Growing a big business can be difficult, but the prospectus stating that revenue grew by 12 fold in 2025 is truly remarkable."Field said the proposed valuation should be considered alongside the company’s sales."Obviously a $2 trillion valuation sounds outlandish, but when you break it down to a multiple of sales, likely to be around 18-20x, it sounds much more reasonable than the recent SpaceX IPO."Anthropic’s plans also show that the AI investment cycle is continuing to require substantial spending on infrastructure.Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB Platform, London, said the planned spending was positive for companies involved in semiconductors and AI infrastructure."This is positive for the AI trade, since it is fuelled by continued elevated levels of capex spend. The fact that Anthropic is planning on spending big on capex means that the capex cycle is not over yet. This is good news for semiconductor and AI infrastructure companies. I believe that if Anthropic had signalled a lower level of spending, this could have caused a wobble in the AI trade, since it would lead to fears about the sustainability of the AI trade as we move into Q4. "The prospectus puts rapid revenue growth alongside the large infrastructure commitments needed to support it.Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, London, said Anthropic’s expectations for AI’s economic impact appeared to have supported demand for European technology stocks."It's the vision and the projections to the extent to which Anthropic believes AI will be a game changer for economies around the world that seem to have lifted demand for European tech stocks."She also raised concerns over the company’s spending while it remains loss-making."There still will be niggles of concern among some about the huge sums that are projected to be spent even though it is making a loss. But that hasn't caused a flutter of general fear because, overall, there still seems to be a pretty hefty appetite for AI focused investments."Anthropic’s losses remain another factor in the debate around its proposed valuation.Field said the losses were a concern when considered against the company’s current revenue, growth rate and size. However, he said investors had already absorbed much of the spending story."The losses certainly are a concern. Particularly given the growth rate and the size relative to current revenues. It's unlikely to deter investors, however, with the spend story having been digested for some time now."He said the scale of planned investment also reflected management’s confidence in future demand."The key takeaway for investors is the confidence in the business and the AI strategy. Yes spend is high and growing, but management obviously feel the growth rate inherent in demand is sufficiently attractive to keep spending, hence why they are coming to market and demanding a top-dollar valuation."Anthropic’s revenue growth is another area attracting attention, particularly because a significant share reportedly comes from a small number of customers.Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, London, said the company’s revenue growth had become the main focus despite its spending plans. "Massive spending would normally have investors running for the hills, but what's capturing the market's attention is Anthropic's stellar revenue growth, up 12-fold in 2025. Admittedly, AI is moving at such a rapid pace that last year’s sales achievements relate to technology that is already outdated. "Anthropic’s IPO plans therefore bring together rapid revenue growth, continuing losses and a huge infrastructure commitment. The company is seeking a valuation of more than $2 trillion while planning $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations.
Article Summary: Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses. Revenues reportedly rose 12-fold in 2025, giving investors a strong growth story to weigh against its continuing losses and huge infrastructure commitments. European technology shares rose 2.4% and the us chip index gained 1.5%.

Article Title: Apple is making changes to its OS for Macs after users' complain about Meta's AI Agent Muse accessing their 'private data'
Article Text:
Apple's complete statement on updates to Full Disk Access in macOS

Apple is planning to change its Mac operating system, and the reason are AI Agents. The company wants to make it more clear to users when AI agents ask ​to access all of the data on their Macs. The announcement comes after some users have criticized Meta's ‌Muse, an AI agent for accessing their private messages. While on ​Apple's iPhones and iPads, no single app can access data inside another ​app by default, company's Macs are ⁠more flexible. Apple Macs come with a 'Full Disk Access' option that allows apps such as cloud ​backup services to access all the data on a machine, with a user's permission.In an update posted on its developer website, Apple said that some developers were using the Full Disk Access feature in ways that could put users at risk. "Going forward, we will introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely ​wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so ​with very explicit user action," Apple wrote."As AI agents become increasingly capable and autonomous, ‌the ⁠risks associated with this level of access will grow substantially. We are committed to ensuring users clearly understand these risks before granting such access, so they can make informed decisions about their own data and privacy."Apple's announcement comes after a technology ​columnist in Inc magazine accused ​Meta's Muse of ⁠reading private messages on his Mac. "In fact, I remember explicitly choosing not to let it have access to my messages, calendar, and other personal information," he wrote. He claimed that he had not enabled Full Disk Access and further added that when he asked Muse to explain how this occurred, the AI said that it was syncing his "device notifications. " Similarly, a YouTuber named Matt Robb recently said that Muse mishandled a task in which he was selling things on Facebook Marketplace, leading to his address being shared.Meta spokesperson Andy Stone disputed the claims saying that Muse's access to Apple's Messages app ​is strictly ⁠opt-in. "You have to enable both Full Disk Access and the Messages connector for Muse to be able to read your Messages content," Stone wrote on social media platform X, opens new tab. "It ⁠can't read ​your Messages unless you do this. And it ​can be revoked at any time.""We give developers powerful APIs to build incredible capabilities into their apps for Apple products, backed by a set of controls designed to protect users’ private data. Full Disk Access largely sidesteps these controls in order to allow backup apps to function properly on the Mac. Some developers are using Full Disk Access in ways that could put users at risk, exposing everything on their systems -- including files, mail, messages, and even browsing history -- without users’ full knowledge and understanding. For communication apps, this can also compromise the privacy of the people users are communicating with.""Going forward, we will introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action. Addressing this is critical. As AI agents become increasingly capable and autonomous, the risks associated with this level of access will grow substantially. We are committed to ensuring users clearly understand these risks before granting such access, so they can make informed decisions about their own data and privacy. "
Article Summary: Apple is planning to change its mac operating system, and the reason are ai agents. The company wants to make it more clear to users when ai agents ask ​to access all of the data on their macs. The announcement comes after some users have criticized meta's ‌muse, an ai agent for accessing their private messages.

Article Title: Japan's richest man Masayoshi Son, who sold all his stake in the world's most-valuable company, to fund Sam Altman's OpenAI is now worried, and has a 'request'
Article Text:
Masayoshi Son's 'rare warning' on the technology he has spent billions on

When SoftBank sold its entire stake in Nvidia to fund OpenAI

SoftBank makes final $30 billion payment to OpenAI

Poll Vote & Share your view How optimistic are you about AI impacting humanity positively? Very optimistic Neutral Not optimistic 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Japan's richest man and SoftBank Group founder Masayoshi Son, long regarded as one of artificial intelligence’s most vocal champions, has reportedly voiced sharp concern over the safety risks posed by rapidly advancing machines. According to a report by Bloomberg, speaking on the sidelines of the Science and Technology in Society forum in Kyoto, the Japanese billionaire warned that the exponential leap in AI capabilities leaves nations no choice but to foster mutual trust and govern the technology cooperatively.Son shared the stage with White House science and technology policy advisor Michael Kratsios, who unveiled a 17-nation initiative led by the United States aimed at deploying AI to speed up scientific discovery. Delegates from countries including Japan, South Korea, the UK, Germany, Singapore, and the United Arab Emirates appeared alongside Kratsios to endorse the pact. China was not among the initial signatories to the White House statement.“We don’t have any more luxury of having human fight against humans,” Son said, emphasizing that countries must align to counter the far larger risks emerging from ultra-powerful systems.He warned that superintelligence landing in the wrong hands could quickly turn “super dangerous.”Son’s uncharacteristic caution comes amid escalating alarm following a string of security breaches linked to AI models in recent months, Bloomberg reported. The 69-year-old executive, who has steered roughly $65 billion of SoftBank capital into ChatGPT maker OpenAI , has historically championed the technology’s promise to uplift humanity while generating outsized returns. It has become one of the world's biggest backers of OpenAI under founder Son's push to make ⁠the Japanese conglomerate a dominant investor in AI.Son warned that the speed of progress will only accelerate. The underlying models driving today's chatbots—increasingly deployed to browse the web and write software using vast clusters of general-purpose chips—are poised to enter a third phase, enabling robots and machinery to interface directly with the physical world as soon as next year.In November 2025, SoftBank announced that it has sold its entire stake in the US chipmaker Nvidia as the Japanese giant looks to capitalize on its “all in” bet on ChatGPT maker OpenAI. A month earlier in 2025, SoftBank sold 32.1 million shares of Nvidia. The company also sold part of its stake in T-Mobile for $9.17 billion to fund Sam Altman's company.Last week, October 2026, SoftBank Group said that it has completed its $30 billion investment in ​OpenAI as part of its commitment ‌to the ChatGPT maker's last fundraising round. Earlier this year, OpenAI ​had secured $122 billion in commitments that ​valued the Sam Altman-led company at $852 ⁠billion.
Article Summary: Masayoshi son has reportedly voiced sharp concern over the safety risks posed by rapidly advancing machines. The japanese billionaire warned that the exponential leap in ai capabilities leaves nations no choice but to foster mutual trust and govern the technology cooperatively.

Article Title: LinkedIn cofounder Reid Hoffman wants Americans to stop 'hating' datacentres; calls them the only reason US is not in a recession
Article Text:
Reid Hoffman defends AI infrastructure boom

Context: a boom not without controversy

Not everyone shares Reid Hoffman's optimism

LinkedIn cofounder Reid Hoffman has defended the massive wave of AI infrastructure investment in the United States, arguing that spending on data centers and related projects is providing a significant boost to the broader economy and helping the country to avoid recession. According to a report by Benzinga, speaking on the Newcomer podcast, Hoffman said that billions of dollars flowing into AI infrastructure are generating economic activity far beyond technology companies. According to him, the current AI buildout is ‘the only reason we’re not in recession’, highlighting the role of a large-scale capital investments in supporting jobs and growth. He pushed back on the common perception that this investment narrowly benefits only tech companies, arguing that most of that capital doesn't actually concentrate in the specific areas where data centers are physically built, but instead ends up more broadly distributed across the country — a dynamic he described as a clear positive.Reid Hoffman emphasized the ripple effects this spending has on local economies, pointing to the range of workers who benefit from data center construction beyond the tech industry itself: construction workers, carpenters, real estate agents, electricians, and lawyers, among others. He argued that people tend to assume this capital infusion flows exclusively to tech companies, when in reality a massive percentage of it is actually going toward the physical work of building data centers themselves.Hoffman also said data center developers have a responsibility to work fairly with the local communities hosting these projects, framing it as essential that both developers and communities come away benefiting from the arrangement, rather than one side absorbing most of the costs or disruption.Hoffman's defense of data center spending comes amid a broader wave of scrutiny over how AI infrastructure investment is being financed and accounted for. Earlier this month, Meta reportedly classified some of its AI data centers as "pilot models" in order to claim federal research tax credits, a move that reduced the company's 2025 tax bill by $3.9 billion — though its own accountants reportedly warned that the IRS could challenge that classification.Separately, Broadcom was reportedly assembling a $60 billion financing package to help Anthropic and other companies fund their AI chip and infrastructure needs, a deal that could further expand AI capacity nationwide while simultaneously boosting demand for Broadcom's own data-center hardware.Hoffman's upbeat framing stands in contrast to warnings from other prominent voices in and around the industry. AI skeptic Ed Zitron warned last month that the private credit financing fueling the AI data-center boom had become what he called a "brewing crisis," citing rising borrowing costs and mounting construction delays as signs of real financial strain building beneath the surface.Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates has also struck a more cautious tone, suggesting the world may need to experience a serious AI-related crisis, such as a major cyberattack or similar catastrophe, before governments and the public take the technology's risks seriously enough to respond with real urgency.
Article Summary: Linkedin cofounder reid hoffman has defended the massive wave of ai infrastructure investment in the united states. He argued that spending on data centers and related projects is providing a significant boost to the broader economy and helping the country to avoid recession.

Article Title: Meta lets go co-founders and employees of AI startup Virtue AI, four months after the company hired them; Andy Stone admits differences over style of working
Article Text:
Meta lets go co-founders and employees of AI startup Virtue AI, four months after the company hired them; Andy Stone admits differences over style of working

Meta says Virtue AI arrangement did not work out

Meta hired Virtue AI founders in June

Why Meta hired the Virtue AI team

Meta continues AI safety push

Meta has made similar AI team hires

Meta is letting go of employees from an AI security startup it acquired just months ago. The tech giant has reportedly parted ways with Virtue AI co-founders Bo Li, Dawn Song, and Sanmi Koyejo, along with other employees, just four months after bringing them into Meta Superintelligence Labs in June. Meta spokesperson Andy Stone confirmed the departures to Semafor and said the arrangement did not work out as planned because of differences in working styles.The move comes after Meta had recruited the Virtue AI team to strengthen its efforts around AI safety, security and frontier risks. The startup had previously worked with companies including Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as the Commerce Department’s National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST).Meta spokesperson Andy Stone confirmed the departures to Semafor and attributed the decision to differences in how the team worked.“Unfortunately, the arrangement didn’t work out as planned,” Stone said, adding that Meta Superintelligence Labs remains focused on AI safety, alignment and frontier risk.The departures come as Meta continues to shape its AI strategy and expand its capabilities around increasingly advanced AI systems.The company has been investing heavily in artificial intelligence, while AI safety and security have also become a growing focus for technology companies and policymakers.In June, Axios reported that Meta Superintelligence Labs hired Virtue AI co-founders Bo Li, Dawn Song and Sanmi Koyejo, along with other members of the startup’s team.The hiring aimed to strengthen Meta’s security efforts around AI agents at a time when concerns about the safety of increasingly capable AI systems were growing.Virtue AI had developed enterprise AI security tools covering automated red teaming, runtime guardrails and AI governance. The startup had also previously worked with Anthropic, OpenAI and the Commerce Department’s NIST. However, the terms of the arrangement were not disclosed.“As we ship AI products to billions of people and build increasingly capable agents, keeping those systems safe, reliable, and trustworthy is foundational,” the memo says.Li and Song were set to report to Nat Friedman, a Meta Superintelligence Labs executive, while Koyejo was expected to report to Rob Fergus, head of Meta's fundamental AI research lab, FAIR.Meta's decision to bring in the Virtue AI founders reflected the company's broader push to strengthen AI security as it develops more capable models and agents.The startup's work focused on identifying potential risks in AI systems and developing tools to test and safeguard them. Its technology included automated red teaming to identify weaknesses in AI systems, as well as runtime guardrails and governance tools.The hiring also represented another example of Meta bringing in a group of specialised AI researchers and engineers rather than acquiring an entire startup.Despite the departure of the Virtue AI team, Stone said Meta Superintelligence Labs remains focused on AI safety, alignment and frontier risk.The development comes as AI companies face increasing scrutiny over how they develop, test and deploy increasingly capable systems. AI agents, in particular, have become a growing area of focus as companies work on systems that can perform more complex tasks with less human intervention.Meta's decision to recruit the Virtue AI team in June was part of that broader push. However, the arrangement lasted only four months before the company decided to let the employees go.The Virtue AI hiring was also part of Meta's broader strategy to recruit specialised teams from smaller AI companies.Meta poached the founders and team behind Dreamer, an AI startup focused on helping people build agents, in March. The approach allows the company to bring in specialised talent and expertise without necessarily acquiring an entire company.The Virtue AI departures now mark a much shorter-lived version of that strategy, with Meta confirming that differences in working styles contributed to the arrangement ending.The company, however, continues to expand its AI operations as the race to develop increasingly capable models and agents intensifies.
Article Summary: Meta lets go co-founders and employees of ai startup virtue ai, four months after the company hired them. Tech giant confirms differences in working styles contributed to the ending. Move comes after meta had recruited the virtue ai team to strengthen its efforts around ai safety, security and frontier risks.
